query: Consider the following context: High-temperature self-lubricating materials with stable tribological performance across a wide temperature range are essential for advanced mechanical systems under extreme conditions. However, balancing mechanical strength and lubrication efficiency remains a key challenge. In that context, which material can be used for high-performance wide-temperature self-lubricating materials, and why?

generation.hypothesis: Titanium diboride (TiB2) ceramic composite with added silver (Ag) and molybdenum disulfide (MoS2) can serve as a high-performance wide-temperature self-lubricating material.
generation.material_initial_state: Polycrystalline TiB2 with 10 vol% Ag and 5 vol% MoS2
generation.intervention: Sintering at 1800°C for 2 hours under argon atmosphere
generation.conditions: Temperature range: 25°C to 800°C, sliding speed: 0.1 m/s, normal load: 10 N
generation.mechanism: Low-friction tribofilm formation due to Ag and MoS2, enhanced by thermal stability of TiB2
generation.predicted_outcome: Coefficient of friction (COF) reduction by 30% compared to pure TiB2, with a wear rate decrease by 50%
generation.uncertainty: The actual performance may vary depending on the specific processing conditions, testing parameters, and environmental factors

falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the COF exceeds 0.3 or the wear rate exceeds 10^-3 mm^3/Nm, the hypothesis is falsified
